title: Evaluating a Deterministic Validator Plus Single‑Iteration Repair Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (N=300 paired intent→configuration tasks; preregistration id cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) to evaluate whether a minimal guarded pipeline—single‑shot LLM generation (declared model: gpt-5-mini) followed by a frozen deterministic configuration validator and at most one automated repair iteration—reduces first‑pass misconfiguration relative to plain single‑shot generation. Execution completed 600 episodes using 301 model calls. Observed outcomes: baseline = 299/300 valid (99.667%); guarded = 300/300 valid (100.0%); paired counts n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single permitted automated repair corrected the sole invalid baseline output (repair success 1/1; Clopper–Pearson 95% CI = [0.025, 1.0]). The preregistered planning assumption used for power calculations (planned baseline pass rate = 0.40) was contradicted by the observed near‑ceiling baseline, removing statistical headroom for the preregistered ≥50% relative‑reduction target. We report preregistered design choices, execution accounting, confirmatory statistics, a post‑hoc inferential sensitivity bound tied to the observed contingency counts, and artifact‑grounded recommendations for future NetOps confirmatory evaluations. All run artifacts and analysis outputs are archived in the execution manifest referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Translating operator intent into device configuration is a core NetOps task. Large language models (LLMs) can synthesize configuration artifacts from high‑level intent, but probabilistic generation risks misordering, omission, and unsafe commands. Recent literature advocates hybrid patterns that pair probabilistic generators with deterministic validators/simulators and bounded repair loops as operational floor‑safety nets. Despite architectural proposals and demonstrations, rigorous preregistered evaluations that quantify how tightly bounded guarded pipelines change first‑pass misconfiguration rates under controlled sampling semantics remain limited. We executed a narrowly scoped, preregistered paired experiment to measure the incremental effect of a frozen deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair iteration on first‑pass validity of LLM proposals. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired experiment (cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) with deterministic seeds and archived per‑task artifacts; (2) confirmatory statistics derived from those artifacts; (3) an artifact‑grounded sensitivity bound tied to the observed discordant count; and (4) pragmatic, artifact‑based recommendations for designing future NetOps confirmatory evaluations.
sections.related_work: Recent system demonstrations and surveys document effective intent→configuration synthesis in lab settings while also cataloging generator failure modes (misordering, omission, overconfidence) that threaten operational safety [10.1002/nem.2313]. Work in adjacent domains shows that verifier‑assisted and retrieval‑augmented pipelines reduce factual errors and improve grounding, motivating guarded architectures for NetOps [10.36227/techrxiv.176784505.56675782/v1, 10.2139/ssrn.6608518]. Deterministic network verification techniques (e.g., header‑space and specification‑based checking) provide algorithmic foundations for validators that can statically check reachability and policy constraints without live device execution [10.1145/3098822.3098834]. Policy and standards reviews emphasize auditability and human‑oversight as open challenges for automated NetOps workflows [10.6028/nist.ai.100-2e2023]. Our experiment sits at the intersection of these strands by producing a preregistered, artifact‑archived measurement of first‑pass validity under a frozen validator+bounded repair policy.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and hypotheses: The experiment was preregistered (cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) before observing outcomes. Confirmatory hypotheses: H1 — the guarded pipeline reduces first‑pass misconfiguration rate by ≥50% (relative) versus single‑shot generation; H2 — one or fewer automated repair iterations recover ≥75% of initially invalid configurations. The preregistration documented the planning assumption baseline pass rate = 0.40 used in power calculations; we report that assumption in Methods because its contradiction by observed data materially alters confirmatory interpretation.

Design and sampling semantics: We used a paired within‑task design with a deterministic seed list of 300 tasks. For each seed the pipeline produced a single shared candidate configuration (shared_initial_candidate semantics) that served as the baseline response and as the starting point for guarded validation and potential repair. Planned episodes = 600 (two episodes per seed), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. The shared‑candidate design intentionally isolates the incremental effect of deterministic validation and bounded repair on one proposed plan; this increases ecological validity for remediation workflows but increases within‑pair correlation and limits discordant pairs available for paired tests.

Model, provider policy, and sampling determinism: The declared generation model was gpt-5-mini. Model configuration recorded during execution shows temperature = null in the archived execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Because temperature was unset (null) in the archived configuration, explicit sampling determinism was not fixed by the contract; provider default sampling semantics therefore determine realized nondeterminism. We therefore state explicitly that sampling determinism is unspecified by the experiment (temperature unset) and discuss inferential implications in Results/Discussion: without a fixed deterministic sampling parameter, identical prompt/model calls could be nondeterministic under provider defaults, but the execution manifest shows provider_call_audit with cache_miss_count=301 and only the preregistered single repair invocation, indicating the actual run used one shared candidate per pair under the recorded provider interactions.

Validator, canonicalization, and repair adapter: The frozen deterministic validator canonicalized generated outputs to a normalized AST and applied explicit static checks encoded from task payload workflow policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, minimum_active_in_groups). The scoring rule labeled success only when the normalized_configuration satisfied the task's required_sequence and expected_final_state and no violation codes remained. The preregistered repair adapter received structured violation codes and the shared candidate and was restricted to a single automated repair attempt per episode; post‑repair outputs were revalidated by the same deterministic validator. Repair prompts, responses, and validator traces were archived per episode and used for conditional repair effectiveness estimation.

Analysis plan and artifacts: The primary estimand was the absolute paired success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline). The preregistered primary test was the exact McNemar two‑sided test (α=0.05) on paired binary outcomes; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CIs for the absolute paired difference were preregistered (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Contamination detection, exclusion rules, and missingness policies were preregistered and executed; all artifacts (task manifest, raw responses, validator traces, paired contingency table) are archived in the execution manifest and analysis bundle and constitute the authoritative source for numerical counts reported below.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact‑derived): Planned episodes = 600; completed episodes = 600; complete pairs analyzed = 300. Model calls used = 301 (300 shared initial generations + 1 repair invocation). No provider or infrastructure failures occurred under the preregistered retry policy; no deterministic exclusions for contamination were applied.

Primary outcome counts (archived): Baseline_success_count = 299/300 (99.667%); Guarded_success_count = 300/300 (100.0%). Paired contingency (guarded vs baseline) from the archived paired_contingency_table.csv is: n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (paired_contingency_table.csv sha256: 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55). These counts are reproduced in the analysis artifacts and are the basis of confirmatory inference.

Inferential results (preregistered): Exact McNemar two‑sided test on the observed contingency gives p = 1.00. Observed absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = (n10 − n01)/N = 1/300 ≈ 0.0033333. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute paired difference = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap seed = 1729; bootstrap parameters are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Repair outcomes (H2): the single automated repair invocation corrected the sole invalid baseline output (repair success 1/1); Clopper–Pearson 95% CI for 1/1 = [0.025, 1.0], reflecting wide uncertainty because only one repair case was observed.

Why p = 1.00 occurred: exact McNemar inference conditions on the observed discordant total (n10 + n01). With only one discordant pair (n10 + n01 = 1), the exact two‑sided test enumerates the small set of possible reassigned discordant outcomes and yields a non‑small p for our observed outcome; the paired bootstrap CI and the contingency counts better summarize effect magnitude and uncertainty in this near‑ceiling baseline regime. The archived paired_contingency_table.csv and bootstrap seed/resample settings allow independent reproduction of these inferential artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Artifact‑grounded interpretation. The archived contingency (n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0) imposes a hard limit on resolvable absolute paired differences: with N=300 the largest resolvable absolute improvement given a single net discordant pair is 1/300 ≈ 0.00333. Our preregistered planning assumption (baseline pass rate = 0.40) therefore diverged sharply from reality (observed baseline = 299/300), eliminating statistical headroom for detecting the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction in failure rate. This mismatch is the primary reason the confirmatory H1 test could not produce evidence for the preregistered large relative effect; the archival artifacts make this arithmetic explicit and reproducible.

Sampling determinism implication. The archived model configuration recorded temperature = null (execution/model_configuration.json sha256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Because temperature was unset, the execution contract did not fix sampling determinism; realized nondeterminism is therefore determined by provider defaults. Practically, unset temperature plus shared_initial_candidate semantics implies the experiment relied on a single generated candidate per seed as executed and archived, but future confirmatory designs should either fix deterministic sampling parameters or explicitly account for provider nondeterminism in power planning and replication protocols.

Design recommendations grounded in artifacts. (1) When the objective is to measure remediation effectiveness of a single plan (shared_candidate semantics), calibrate task difficulty or adversarially augment tasks to produce a nontrivial baseline failure prevalence or a preregistered target discordant‑pair count that matches planned absolute effect sizes. (2) When repair effectiveness is a target estimand, power the study for expected number of initial failures (not merely overall N); conditional estimands like P(repair succeeds | initial failure) require a planned number of failure cases for precise CI estimation. (3) When runtime semantics matter, integrate emulation or simulation validation stages and preregister how emulator outcomes map to success/failure so that construct validity extends beyond static checks. These recommendations are traceable to task difficulty fields, validator violation codes, and the paired contingency artifact in the execution bundle.

Limitations specific to interpretation. The experiment uses a synthetic task bank and a single validator and model declaration (gpt-5-mini), limiting external generality. Validation used deterministic static checks rather than full dynamic emulation of control‑plane/dataplane behavior; reported success counts are therefore conditional on validator coverage. The single observed repair case yields a highly uncertain conditional repair effectiveness estimate. These substantive limitations are enumerated in the manuscript's Limitations section and in the archived manifest.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired experiment (300 pairs) comparing single‑shot LLM generation (declared model gpt-5-mini) to a guarded pipeline consisting of a frozen deterministic validator and a single automated repair iteration. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 valid outputs; the guarded pipeline produced 300/300 valid outputs. The single automated repair corrected the lone invalid baseline output, but the observed near‑ceiling baseline contradicted the preregistered planning assumption (baseline pass rate = 0.40) and removed statistical headroom to detect the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction. Future confirmatory NetOps evaluations should (a) calibrate task difficulty or adversarially augment tasks to ensure sufficient initial failures or discordant counts for planned effect sizes, (b) preregister pairing semantics and sampling determinism explicitly (e.g., fix temperature or record provider default behavior), and (c) include emulation when runtime semantics are essential. All raw outputs, validator traces, repair traces, the execution manifest, and analysis artifacts are archived and enumerated in the Disclosure Statement to permit reproduction of reported counts and intervals.

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role: the Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approved the master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; no manual human editing of manuscript technical content, figures, tables, or references occurred after the lock. Preregistration: cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1 (created before observing final outcomes; preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest). Declared model and tooling: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version), adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1, frozen deterministic validator/repair adapter deterministic_netops_validator_v5.

Model configuration and sampling determinism: The archived execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (sha256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Because temperature was unset (null) in the archived configuration, the execution contract did not fix sampling determinism; realized nondeterminism is therefore determined by provider defaults. The manuscript explicitly reports this artifact value and states that sampling determinism is unspecified by the experiment; the provider call audit in the execution manifest documents actual provider interactions (hosted_model_call_event_count = 301, cache_miss_count = 301, repair stage_count = 1).

Execution accounting (archived): planned episodes = 600, completed episodes = 600, complete pairs = 300, model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared initial generation calls + 1 repair invocation), repair-stage invocations = 1. The execution manifest and analysis artifact bundle enumerate all raw model responses, per‑task validator traces (normalized configurations, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, repair_applied flags), repair prompts/responses, execution logs, and analysis artifacts. Paired contingency artifact: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha256: 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55). Bootstrap parameters used for CI computation: 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729 (recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Preregistration and interpretive caveat: The preregistered H1 hypothesis required a planning assumption baseline pass rate = 0.40 used in power calculations. The observed baseline pass rate (299/300 ≈ 0.9967) contradicted that assumption and removed statistical headroom for the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction target; therefore H1 could not be meaningfully tested as a confirmatory large‑effect hypothesis given the observed data. The manuscript reports this fact explicitly in Methods, Results, and here in the Disclosure Statement and limits confirmatory claim language accordingly.

Reproducibility: The execution manifest, per‑task artifacts, and analysis bundle in the archived run are the authoritative sources for all numeric counts and inferential inputs reported in this paper. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search, preregistration, execution, analysis, AI‑peer‑review style checks, and manuscript drafting autonomously after the autonomy lock in accordance with the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track requirements. Pre‑lock development artifacts were used only for infrastructure rehearsal and are not reported as empirical evidence for the final study.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and constrained vendor‑template scope limit external validity to broad production environments.
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini declaration) and single validator implementation restrict generality across model families and validator designs.

The preregistered power plan assumed a baseline pass rate = 0.40; the observed baseline (299/300) contradicted that assumption and removed headroom to detect the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction.
Sampling semantics (shared_initial_candidate) reused the same initial candidate across paired arms, increasing within‑pair correlation and reducing discordant pairs available to McNemar inference.

Validation used deterministic configuration/constraint checks rather than full dynamic emulation of runtime semantic effects; actual runtime consequences of configurations were not executed and remain unmeasured.

H2 repair‑success evidence is based on a single initially invalid case (1/1 → 100%), yielding a wide Clopper–Pearson 95% CI = [0.025, 1.0]; larger counts of initial failures are required to estimate repair effectiveness precisely.
